page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top. Marginal note "Cap.27." in the right margin beside the line "Medi-". Catchword "medi-" at right below the last line. Signature "O 3" at foot.

main_text.p: chi omne uitium, & præcipuè quod cum fluore confiftit. Facit & ad oculorum epi-phoras,& ad tormina,& ad coli inflatione, iocinoris,pectoris dolorem, tusfietes,ad-uerfus mala medicamenta omnia, ferpen-tium morfus,uel ictus. Oportet autem lo-cum morfum à rabiofo cane, uel à ferpen-te,diu tenere in exulcerationem: neq; pati cicatricem ducere, ut uirus illa perrrahat[?]. Extra itaq; ea funt imponenda, quæ etiam fana corpora exulcerant, ut allium,lepidi-um,chelidonium,batrachium, finapis,fcyl-la,cæpa cum aceto. Optime facit & per fe caprifici liber per fe contritus & impofitus ulceri:ité laser per fe.Hæc Scribonius Lar-gus de Medicamentis aduersus canis rabi-di morfum.Supereft tandē,q de hac re me-dicorū omniū Latinorū princeps, & Hip-pocrat.alter Cornel.Celfus lib.de re Medi-Cap.27.ca 5.pertractauit in luce ꝑ ducere. Vtiq; aut (inqt)si rabiofus canis fuit,cucurbita uirus eius extrahēdū est,deinde si locus neq; ner uofus,neq; musculofus est,uulnus id adure dū est: Si uri non poteft, sanguine homini mitti nō alienum est. page.notes: The running head begins with an ornament before "AVSAS" that I read as a Greek or decorative letter; the first word is doubtful. "perrrahat" appears to be a printing error for "pertrahat"; left as printed. "tusfietes" and "ictus" have a doubtful accent mark over the vowel. Line 1 begins mid-word ("chi"), a fragment from the previous line, kept as printed. The Greek fleuron at the very start of the running head is not transcribed.
